decisions.reason: It is core airfield control hardware in the firm's established integrated offering, and such airport infrastructure products usually have long life cycles and strong installed-base support needs.
A surveillance display fits the firm's push toward real-time information sharing and integrated operations, so it is more likely to be maintained than withdrawn.
Training supports system adoption and customer retention, though service products can be repackaged more easily than hardware or software platforms.
This is a narrower training offer with less standalone visibility, so it has a higher risk of being merged into broader services, but it still supports the installed airfield lighting business.
Airport collaboration software is highly aligned with the firm's stated direction toward integrated, intelligent and collaborative airport operations.
An advanced multilateration surveillance system is a strategic, R&D-intensive product in a growing airport-operations portfolio and is therefore unlikely to be dropped so soon after launch.
